theory.intro: **Skewness** describes how symmetrical a distribution is, and together with modality it describes the distribution's **shape**. Skewness is named from the **tail** — the side on which the columns keep getting shorter and stretch further away from the bulk of the data. So read the display, find where most of the data sits, then see which side trails off.
facts: **Symmetrical**: the left and right halves of the display are close to mirror images, so neither side has a longer tail.
**Negatively skewed**: the tail stretches to the **left**, so most of the data sits on the **right** (some books call this left-skewed).
**Positively skewed**: the tail stretches to the **right**, so most of the data sits on the **left** (some books call this right-skewed).
Name the skew by the **tail**, never by the peak. A distribution whose tallest columns are on the left has its tail on the right, so it is positively skewed.
A distribution does not have to be bell-shaped to be symmetrical — a flat display and a display with two matching peaks can both be symmetrical.

foundation.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.85]\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,4.8);\draw[->] (0,0)--(9,0);\draw[thick] plot[smooth,tension=0.6] coordinates {(0.2,0.05)(1,0.2)(2,0.5)(3,1.1)(4,2)(5,3)(5.8,3.4)(6.6,2.2)(7.4,0.6)(8,0.08)};\node[rotate=90,font=\scriptsize] at (-1.1,1.7) {Frequency};\node[below,font=\scriptsize] at (4,-1.0) {Mark};\node[font=\small] at (4,4.5) {Exam marks};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The curve shows the distribution of the marks of a large group of students on an exam. Describe the shape of this distribution.
foundation.solution_text:
The curve rises slowly from the left over a long stretch and then drops away quickly on the right.
The long, low part of the curve is on the left, so the tail stretches to the left.
Negatively skewed.

foundation.question_text: A very difficult exam was sat by $200$ students. Most students scored low marks and only a few scored high marks. Describe the shape of the distribution of the marks.
foundation.solution_text:
Most of the data sits at the low marks on the left of the display.
The few high marks stretch out to the right.
The tail stretches to the right, so the distribution is positively skewed.

foundation.question_text:
The frequency table shows the marks of $52$ students on an exam.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline \text{Mark} & \text{Frequency} \\ \hline 0\text{--}19 & 2 \\ \hline 20\text{--}39 & 5 \\ \hline 40\text{--}59 & 11 \\ \hline 60\text{--}79 & 20 \\ \hline 80\text{--}100 & 14 \\ \hline \end{array}$
Describe the shape of this distribution.
foundation.solution_text:
The largest frequency is $20$, at $60\text{--}79$, so most of the data sits on the right.
The frequencies fall away over the classes $40\text{--}59$, $20\text{--}39$ and $0\text{--}19$ on the left.
The tail stretches to the left, so the distribution is negatively skewed.

Each curve shows the distribution of a different dataset. Which curve, $A$, $B$ or $C$, is positively skewed?
development.solution_text:
$A$ has its high point near the right and its long, low stretch on the left, so it is negatively skewed.
$B$ is a mirror image on both sides, so it is symmetrical.
$C$ has its high point near the left and its long, low stretch on the right.
Curve $C$.

development.question_text: The weekly incomes of every worker in a large city are recorded. Most workers earn a moderate income, but a small number of people earn very large incomes. Describe the shape of the distribution of the incomes.
development.solution_text:
The bulk of the data sits at the moderate incomes, towards the left of the display.
The small number of very large incomes stretch a long way to the right.
The tail stretches to the right, so the distribution is positively skewed.

development.question_text:
The frequency table shows the weekly incomes of $100$ workers.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline \text{Weekly income (\$)} & \text{Frequency} \\ \hline 0\text{--}499 & 26 \\ \hline 500\text{--}999 & 41 \\ \hline 1000\text{--}1499 & 18 \\ \hline 1500\text{--}1999 & 9 \\ \hline 2000\text{--}2499 & 4 \\ \hline 2500\text{--}2999 & 2 \\ \hline \end{array}$
Describe the shape of this distribution.
development.solution_text:
The largest frequency is $41$, in the second class, so most of the data sits on the left.
The frequencies fall away through $18, 9, 4, 2$ across the classes to the right.
The tail stretches to the right, so the distribution is positively skewed.

mastery.solution_text:
The column heights are $3, 9, 4, 4, 9, 3$, which read the same forwards and backwards, so neither side has a longer tail.
There are two peaks, at $20$ and at $50$, separated by a dip.
Bimodal and symmetrical.

Every column has the same height, so the display is flat and there are no peaks; the distribution is uniform.
A tail is a side on which the columns keep getting shorter, and neither side does, so there is no tail.
With no tail on either side the two halves are mirror images, so the distribution is symmetrical.
